youtube.title: A Generated Event Bus Over gRPC — Publish/Subscribe in Every Language | grpc-over-datachannels
youtube.description:
eventbus-grpc is a generated publish/subscribe event bus on top of grpc-over-datachannels: a broker service with tag-filtered subscriptions and per-subscriber sequence numbers, exposed through the same generated clients used for gRPC — native and browser. It ships as its own repository with its own packages next to grpc-dc and kafka-grpc.

Code: https://github.com/browser-grpc/eventbus
Main project: https://github.com/browser-grpc/grpc-over-datachannels

Built with Fish Audio

scenes.heading: An Event Bus, Generated
scenes.sub: Publish and subscribe, over the same generated gRPC.
scenes.say: Every project eventually grows a pub sub bus, usually as glue nobody wants to maintain. This is an event bus generated the same way as the g R P C runtimes themselves: one service definition, clients in every generated language, browser included.

scenes.heading: Why another bus?
bullets: Services need events without a heavyweight broker deploy
Browser clients are second-class in most messaging stacks
The glue code is small, repeated, and easy to get subtly wrong
scenes.say: Not every system earns a dedicated broker deployment, and browser clients are second-class citizens in most messaging stacks. The glue each team writes instead is small, repeated everywhere, and easy to get subtly wrong. Generate it once, properly.

scenes.heading: Broker, filters, sequences
bullets: Publish events with string tags; subscribe with tag filters
Each subscriber sees a gap-free per-subscriber sequence
Broker stats expose publish, deliver, and drop counts
scenes.say: The broker is a generated service. Publishers attach string tags to events; subscribers open a stream with tag filters and receive only what matches. Every subscriber sees its own gap-free sequence of events, and the broker reports what it published, delivered, and dropped.

scenes.heading: Same clients, same transports
bullets: Runs over the transports the runtime already generates
DataChannel, sidecar, and plain socket paths all carry it
Native servers and browser clients mix freely
scenes.say: The bus rides the transports the runtime already generates, so the same generated client that calls your services also publishes and subscribes, from a native process or a browser tab. Servers and clients mix across languages, because underneath, it is all the same generated wire.

scenes.heading: Its own packages
bullets: Dedicated eventbus repository and package set
Published next to grpc-dc and kafka-grpc, per language
Consumed like any other generated service, no vendoring
scenes.say: The event bus ships as its own repository with its own packages, next to the core and Kafka package sets, in each language's package manager. You depend on it the way you depend on the runtime itself, and generated code stays generated, never vendored by hand.

scenes.heading: Live: filtered subscription over one channel
scenes.say: Here it is live. One subscriber, filtered to the orders topic; three events published; the two that match arrive in order, the noise does not. The broker's counters say exactly what happened.

scenes.heading: Find it
bullets: Demos generated in every language tree
scenes.say: The bus has its own home, its own packages, and a generated demo in every language tree. If your services already speak generated g R P C, they can already publish. Links are in the description.
